Michael Strahan Bought This Dodge Challenger SRT Demon in 2023, Drove 350 Miles, Listed It for Sale
30 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
This car was "built especially for Michael Strahan." This is what the window sticker shows. Ordered directly by the Hall of Fame defensive end, this 2023 Dodge Challenger SRT Demon 170 Jailbreak Last Call (good luck remembering this designation!) is a one-of-one machine. Its one and only owner so far drove only 347 miles and listed it for sale.
What sets this Demon 170 apart from any other Demon 170 on the planet is a mix of exclusivity. So, first things first. The car features a custom factory plaque and serial number #00092, specially chosen by the NFL star to match the jersey number he wore throughout his entire 15-year career with the New York Giants.
Available by invitation only to an elite group of VIP customers, the Challenger Demon 170 Jailbreak Last Call was the swan song of an entire generation of muscle cars and cost an additional $29,995 on a first-come, first-served basis, unlocking access to 40 exclusive paint colors. This means that out of the entire production run, this is the sole example finished in Dark Green (paint code F8).
It features aggressively styled Satin Black graphics across the hood, roof, decklid, and taillight panel, while the Air Grabber hood carries the "Alcohol Injected" lettering. The Dodge Challenger SRT Demon 170 Jailbreak Last Call rides on Lacks Enterprises carbon fiber wheels, measuring 18 inches up front and 17 inches out back, wrapped in street-legal, drag-ready Mickey Thompson tires.
Photo: Bring a Trailer Michael Strahan's Challenger SRT Demon 170 comes with factory “01 of 01” and “Last Call” plaques, while another under the hood and the window sticker indicate that it was "built especially for Michael Strahan." He paid $162,836 to go home with it, with over $88,000 in factory options.
The option list includes the heated and ventilated front seats in Black Alcantara and Laguna leather with Demonic Red seatbelts, the Alcantara-wrapped multifunction steering wheel with shift paddles, and the plush suede headliner and door panel accents.
The 18-speaker Harman Kardon surround sound system, backed by a GreenEdge amplifier and a trunk-mounted subwoofer, is also on the list, as if the HEMI-diehard driver would ever need any other soundtrack outside that provided by the HEMI orchestra.
However, he didn't really enjoy it much, because now, three years after delivery, it only has 347 miles (558 kilometers) on the clock, which makes it a pristine, collector-grade machine that still has the factory yellow scuff guards attached to the front splitter and protective plastic foil on the screens inside the cabin.
Photo: Bring a Trailer Strahan probably saw it as an investment right from the get-go, hoping to cash in one day. That is such a pity, considering that the Demon 170 is the most powerful road-going car that Dodge has ever built before pulling the plug on the almighty HEMI and the cars that came with it.
..
That almighty 6.2-liter HEMI V8 works alongside a massive 3.0-liter supercharger with a 3.02” pulley and a 105-millimeter throttle body to pump out a mind-blowing 1,025 horsepower (1,039 metric horsepower) and 945 pound-feet (1,281 Newton meters) of torque on E85. That’s something that those buying a new-generation Dodge Charger Daytona or a Hurricane-powered Charger can only dream of.
It is a bit tamer when running on regular pump gas, with a factory rating of 900 horsepower (912 metric horsepower) and 810 pound-feet (1,098 Newton meters) of torque. On E85, it rockets from zero to hero (0 to 60 mph or 0 to 97 kph) in just 1.66 seconds, runs the quarter mile in a staggering 8.91 seconds at 151.17 mph (243.28 kph) and maxes out (don't laugh!) at 149 mph (240 kph). Yeah, right.
An eight-speed TorqueFlite automatic transmission puts the power down through the rear wheels in pure muscle car fashion. Black-painted four-piston Brembo brake calipers, sporting the yellow "SRT" lettering over ventilated discs, provide the stopping power. The Demon rides on an edition-specific Drag Mode suspension with adaptive damping shocks and features Launch Control to make it rocket down the strip.
Photo: Bring a Trailer The 2023 Dodge Challenger SRT Demon Jailbreak Last Call is now going with a clean Montana title and a clean Carfax report with no accidents or mileage discrepancies. Who would have thought, right? The winning bidder will get the ultimate collector documentation pack.
The orientation kit brings the color samples of the 40 exclusive paint options available, the custom Demon 170 drinkware set, and the elite wooden presentation chest with the VIN and the owner’s name engraved, housing the printed signatures of the entire Dodge Design Team. The original window sticker and the owner’s manual are also included.
The auction on Bring a Trailer will end on Thursday, November 5. With three days to go, bidding got as far as $89,400. That surely is light-years away from what the owner hopes to get for the HEMI-powered monster that he bought back in 2023 and hardly ever touched.
Hopefully, even though owners prefer to keep such cars low mileage , hoping their value rockets over the years, whoever buys it will track it until its wheels fall off.
